log.msg: Coordinator relay mid-build: deleted an unused v3.css rule (.v3-detail > p margin/line-height, nothing had proven it) per the owner live-watching standard, write no CSS unless a shot needs it -- holding to that for everything added from here. Four V3 features named for a future task, not this one: sticky spatial timeline (new-at-top without moving scroll/selection, a New item button, spacebar jumps to newest), yes/no ask buttons on a card via the append RPC, a per-column toolbar, and resurfacing (a referenced card rises again, see: <id> embeds a small preview) -- appended to requirements.md under For the next V3 task.

Real incident: compose.js (a new shared module) shipped with a wrong relative import depth (two ../ instead of three), and because says.js statically imported it at the dev bar top level, it blanked EVERY page of the owner live site from ~17:00:52 to ~17:02:13 (the mastermind caught it and fixed the three paths). I did not load a page headless before releasing that batch -- the reload hold blocks browser-tab reloads, not the health watchers own independent crawl, and is not a substitute for actually checking. Fixed for real: compose.js now imports ext/Ask/stream.js, ext/Ask/edit.js and ux/Dictate/Dictate.js by ROOT-ABSOLUTE path (/framework/...), not relative depth; says.js no longer statically imports compose.js at all -- it captures a host div synchronously and dynamic-imports compose.js inside a try/catch, appending into the host only once the import resolves, so a future fault in V3-only code can only ever cost the composer, never the whole dev bar / whole site. Verified headless against the mastermind live :8123 server: /framework/, /framework/ai/v/3/, /framework/dev/DevBar/ all zero console/network errors; separately opened the rail with Ctrl+ on / and confirmed the composer mounts via the lazy import with zero errors. Going forward: hold on -> write -> load affected pages headless (zero failed requests, non-empty body) -> hold off, every batch, no exceptions.

assign.outcome:
**Landed, items 1–4 (5–7 cut on the mastermind's call — see below).** ![the timeline inbox: the selected card goes fully white, unselected cards sit a step off-white, status-coloured edges, the owner's own words one click down](shot.png)

1. **The Now view** — first and default at `/framework/ai/v/3/`: the owner's newest words verbatim, in a mono transcription card with the mic icon, and everything answering it growing in live underneath (streaming text nodes, never a re-render). It follows the newest owner message on its own unless you're reading, then offers a "new ↓" chip. Nothing in it is ever clamped.
2. **Heard → answer, merged.** An owner card with an answer (`re:` its id) is now ONE row in the inbox — the answer's own face, with "you said: …" one click down in its detail, styled the same transcription way as the Now view. An unanswered owner card still stands alone. Owner cards no longer print their own text twice (title was always just the first 90 characters of the same text below it).
3. **The composer is wired to the streaming assistant** (`ext/Ask/stream.js`, preset `assistant`) — one shared box (`ai/v/3/compose.js`) mounted at the bottom of the mastermind log (now the dev bar's default tab) AND the Now view. Type or dictate, press Send, and the reply types itself out live in both places — the server writes the owner's words and the growing reply straight to the board, so the box itself only sends.
4. **`chat` is `sessions` now, and it is not the default.** The mastermind log (`says.js`) is the `page` tab's own first section and IS the live view, so the old separate live tab is gone. `sessions` (`history.js`) is HISTORY only — past sessions labelled by their first real words and when they started, a session's minions underneath, test/headless runs hidden by default with a "show test runs" toggle.

**A real incident, disclosed and fixed.** The new shared `compose.js` shipped with a relative import one `../` short, and because the dev bar's `says.js` imported it statically at its own top level, it blanked the owner's ENTIRE live site for about 80 seconds before the mastermind caught and fixed the three paths. Fixed for real, not just patched: `compose.js`'s own cross-tree imports are now root-absolute (`/framework/ext/Ask/...`), and `says.js` no longer imports it statically at all — it dynamic-`import()`s it lazily behind a `try`, so a future fault there can only ever cost the composer, never the rail or the site. Verified headless afterward, zero console/network errors, on `/framework/`, `/framework/ai/v/3/` (all three views, 400/1920px) and the dev bar opened on `/`. One evidence line added to `.claude/skills/code/improvements.md`.

**The CSS audit + the card word (both the owner's mid-task requests, done before landing, not new scope).** Deleted the `.v3-detail > p` rule the owner flagged live. Every `display:flex`/`flex-direction:column`/`gap:var(--gap)`/`padding:var(--pad)` v3.css used to spell out by hand is now the framework's own utility classes in the markup instead (`flex v wrap v-center gap pad grid`). Every tile / inbox card / detail pane now wears `.card` (landed mid-task by the `card-word` sibling) — ground, hairline, `--radius`, `--pad-card`, automatic rhythm between its own children, no flex of its own; the status edge is `.card`'s own `--card-edge` custom property, set inline per card (`edge_of()`, page.js) instead of three bespoke colour classes. Selection went through TWO owner passes: first `.card.selected`'s framework-wide inset ink ring, then the owner rejected that for V3 too, live ("no black border; less white fill that lightens on select") — V3's own cards now sit a step off pure white normally and the SELECTED one is the one that goes fully white, scoped to `.v3-tile` only; `framework.css` itself is untouched, and its own `.card.selected` probably wants the same rethink — noted for the next mastermind, not done here. Also fixed along the way: a real 400px overflow bug (grid-item and flex-item `min-width:auto` letting a long mono line of the owner's own words push off the right edge — `min-width:0` on the two boxes that needed it), a dead-CSS bug (a `gap` utility class silently overriding a smaller hand-tuned gap because utility classes live in a later CSS layer), and a latent dark-mode bug (`var(--paper, #fff)`, a token that was never real, replaced with the actual `--surface` token throughout). v3.css: 222 lines / ~240 declarations before → 256 lines (more comment, explaining why) / ~205 declarations after — a real reduction, not "well under half" by raw line count once the explanatory comments are counted, said honestly rather than rounded up.

**Cut, on the mastermind's explicit call once the incident ate the time budget:** item 5 (the health readout — `ai/health/devbar.js` is built and unwired; the wiring is two lines, named in that module's own doc comment), item 6 (grid polish), item 7 already folded into the card-word migration above. Also cut: the formal private-server (`:8146`, scratch board/ledger) timed proof of the composer's first-chunk latency that the brief's own "Prove" section asks for — verified instead, repeatedly, against the mastermind's live `:8123` server with real board data and a real in-flight assistant reply visible in both the log and the Now view (see the screenshot), which is stronger evidence than a scratch run but is not the same proof the brief specified; a private-server timing run is the one item from the original brief genuinely left undone. The requested full-bleed two-column resizable layout with hour lines is the NEXT task's job (`ai/2026-09-19/v3-timeline/`), not built further here. The dev bar's own log cards (`devbar.css`'s `.dev-says-card`) were NOT swapped to `card size-small` — not a clean swap (different background token, per-author tints, no border wanted) and `devbar.css` is the exact file that caused today's incident — listed for the next task. Four more V3 features the owner named live (sticky spatial timeline, yes/no ask buttons, a per-column toolbar, resurfacing) are written up under "For the next V3 task" in this task's own `requirements.md`, not built here.
